name: Source Inspector
description:
Inspect a source under its kind and report bindable targets, optional operation framing, and completeness information.

These operations are offered for voluntary adoption by name. Their schemas and descriptions identify the exchanged values and the capability they describe; they do not prescribe an SDK, internal algorithm, validation or recovery policy, or process architecture. Correspondence is an author claim, not verification of an implementation.

Sources and bindings are OpenBindings 0.2 values. Their core fields have their core meanings and types; x- members are extensions. Source and binding content preserve absence versus JSON null and are interpreted under the source's exact kind. The open carrier schemas are not complete document-conformance checks. Handling malformed carriers is implementation policy; it does not make those carriers conformant.

SupportedKind.description: A kind supported for the work this interface performs.

kind.description: Exact, opaque kind as carried by a source.

Source.description: A source as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it: an exact kind and optional content read under that kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core source fields and x- extensions may appear; the open carrier schema does not fully check that boundary. Handling malformed carriers is implementation policy.

kind.description: The source's kind, compared by exact equality.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the source has none.

Operation.description: Potential OpenBindings operation framing for a bindable target. Input and output schemas have the core schema and reference meanings they will have in an authored OBI. The inspection response and source artifact supply no implicit schema resource or additional schema map. Portable framing identifies needed resources within the carried schemas or through absolute schema URIs; it does not rely on unspecified members of a future OBI. A schema resource declared with $id can carry its own local references. Framing is optional when those reference meanings cannot be supplied. This describes the framing claim, not a required inlining, bundling, validation or resource-acquisition procedure.

BindableTarget.description: A target admitted by the source kind, with a binding fragment and optional operation framing for that target. The fragment uses core binding fields and x- extensions, without author-assigned operation and source keys. The author supplies those keys when composing a document. Handling malformed fragments is consumer policy.

sourceRef.description: Stable identifier for this target within the observed source. An implementation offering both inspection and synthesis uses the same reference for the same target-scope unit. Equality across producers is meaningful only where the kind defines it. This field does not prescribe duplicate-row handling.

SourceInspection.description: Inventory of targets admitted by the source kind. exhaustive describes completeness of the target inventory; limitation explains a non-exhaustive result. The interface does not prescribe target ordering, duplicate rejection, or deduplication.

exhaustive.description: True when targets is the complete list of targets admitted by the source's kind. False means more admitted targets may exist and requires limitation evidence.

InspectionLimitation.description: Machine-readable evidence explaining why a source inspection is not exhaustive.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what may be missing and why.

details.description: Optional implementation- or kind-specific structured evidence.

KindSupportVerdict.description: Authoritative support verdict for one exact kind. Future optional fields may annotate the verdict but never qualify or soften supported.

kind.description: The exact kind supplied by the caller.

supported.description: True reports that this implementation knows how to interpret this exact kind for its job; it does not promise that every case succeeds. False reports no support for that job.

Binding.description: A binding as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it, or would carry it, by value. It is interpreted under the accompanying source's kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core binding fields and x- extensions may appear; the open carrier schema does not fully check that boundary. Handling malformed carriers is implementation policy.

operation.description: The author's operation key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

source.description: The author's source key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the binding has none.

idempotent.description: The binding author's idempotency claim, carried as information.

preference.description: The author's preference signal, carried as information.

deprecated.description: The author's deprecation signal, carried as information.

openbindings.source-inspector.listSuppor.description: Return an advisory list of kinds supported for this interface's job. Listed kinds have supported: true in checkKindSupport; absence from the list makes no support claim. This is a capability query, not performance of the job.

openbindings.source-inspector.checkKindS.description: Report support for this interface's job for the requested exact kind strings, with one verdict per distinct requested kind in first-occurrence order. supported: true means the implementation knows how to interpret that kind for this job, not that every artifact or case succeeds. supported: false reports no support for that job. Additional fields do not qualify the Boolean. The operation reports capability without performing the requested inspection, synthesis or invocation. Kind equality is the core's exact string equality. Capability detection and representation are implementation choices.

oneKind.description: Illustrative job-specific support query; the example kind is defined for these examples only.

openbindings.source-inspector.inspectSou.description: Inspect a source and return bindable targets admitted by its kind, optionally with operation framing for those same targets. exhaustive reports whether the inventory is complete; a partial result carries limitation evidence. Each target carries a binding fragment without operation or source keys, which the document author supplies. Operation framing has the core operation shape; idempotent is binding metadata. Inspection does not intentionally change the inspected source or perform its operations. Acquisition, enumeration, ordering, duplicate handling and recovery are implementation choices. Editing the source or binding afterward creates a new correspondence claim.

textTargets.description: Illustrative kind example.text@1 has two targets: echo returns its input string, and length counts its Unicode code points. Source content is absent; binding content names the target. These example names and framing choices are not conventions for other kinds.

operation.description: Count Unicode code points in the input string.
